title: SPARCS screen identifies a Golgi-pH regulator of STING signaling
summary: A genome-wide imaging and CRISPR screen of about 70 million cells identified GPR89A and GPR89B (encoding GPHR) as important for maintaining Golgi acidity and early STING trafficking and activation. The study also found a previously undescribed autophagy phenotype associated with EI24 and linked it to altered autophagosome formation.
ai_technology: SPARCS platform with machine-learning image analysis
organization: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, Helmholtz Munich, Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry and Technical University of Munich

evidence.tested: A genome-wide imaging and CRISPR screen of about 70 million cells identified GPR89A and GPR89B (encoding GPHR) as important for maintaining Golgi acidity and early STING trafficking and activation.
evidence.unknown: The study used pools of at least 500 excised cells for sequencing, so it could not map individual images to individual guide RNAs. The paper describes GPHR as a regulator of STING trafficking and signaling; therapeutic implications remain untested.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning image analysis classified phenotypes in genome-wide CRISPR screens; SPARCS recovered known autophagy genes and surfaced EI24 and GPHR-linked findings. Follow-up molecular profiling and experiments by the researchers examined these hits.
